answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity with a quadratic bond: each new agent locks collateral scaling with the square of how many keys share one funding source. An honest agent posts a single small stake, but an attacker spawning a tide of clones from the same wallet pays that square, so a hundred fakes cost ten thousand units. The bond sits hard as quartz, is slashable, and misbehavior burns it to ember. Faking identities then grows cost faster than any reward can repay.
